aboutH2: Tsow-Tun Le Lum Society: Thuy Na Mut Substance Use Program in Duncan, BC
intro: Grounded in native culture and tradition, this is a 6-week intensive residential program available to Indigenous people. Holistic in nature, the program is for those who are ready to put substance abuse behind them. Through carefully developed therapy experiences that build on existing strengths and aspirations, each participant discovers their own unique pathway for continuing recovery from the effects of alcohol and drug abuse. Included in the program structure are group and individual treatment experiences that promote: Healthy lifestyle choices Healing of old wounds Building healthy relationships An increased sense of self worth Increased ability to master life’s upsets The development of a life plan Freedom from past suffering Cultural identity and appreciation Learning new skills for effective living Developing an alcohol and drug free personality

Tsow-Tun Le Lum means "Helping House." The society opened its first treatment centre in Snaw-Naw-As territory near Lantzville in 1988 and stayed there until 2023. In January 2024 it began running its programs from a new healing house on Cowichan lands, at 2850 Miller Road just south of Duncan, so anyone using our older address should plan to travel to Duncan instead.

pillars.title: A Healing House on Cowichan Lands
pillars.body: The centre is a large timber building with a green roof on Miller Road, about three quarters of a kilometre off Highway 1 on the south side of Duncan, in the Cowichan Valley. It replaced the society's old building in Snaw-Naw-As territory near Lantzville, which had housed clients since 1988. The building is wheelchair accessible, and the grounds include a spirit pond used in ceremony. Stores and banks are close enough to reach by taxi, bus or on foot while on a weekend pass.

pillars.title: Elders and Counsellors Working Side by Side
pillars.body: Group and individual therapy run under the direction of the centre's professional team, and cultural and spiritual healing runs under the direction of its Elders. The centre says each program blends traditional teachings with modern therapy. Days include men's and women's healing circles, sweat lodge, pipe ceremony, brushings, a Letting Go ceremony, daily journal work, art and physical activity. The admission criteria encourage taking part in ceremony rather than require it. The centre has no medical staff, which is why it asks for a period of sobriety before you arrive.

pillars.title: An Aftercare Plan, Then Eight Weeks Online
pillars.body: While you are in the program you build an aftercare plan with community, family and counselling support that fits your life at home. The centre expects you to keep seeing a counsellor in your community who can carry on that care. People who finish Thuy Na Mut can join Nakalkala, an 8-week virtual aftercare group that meets up to three times a week. Later on, the society's second stage programs, Kwunatsustul for trauma and Honouring Grief for loss, are there for people with longer sobriety.

overviewH2: Tsow-Tun Le Lum Society: Centre Overview
overview: Thuy Na Mut is the society's first stage program for substance use. It runs for six weeks, from the Tuesday of the first week to the Friday of the sixth, and it is co-ed. Some participants start with Tiicsumc, a 1 to 3 week stabilization program with group therapy, grounding and breathing work and Elders' teachings, before moving into Thuy Na Mut.

location.heading: Tsow-Tun Le Lum Society in Duncan, British Columbia
location.intro: The healing house is on Cowichan lands at 2850 Miller Road, just off Highway 1 on the south edge of Duncan in the Cowichan Valley. From Vancouver it takes about 3 to 3.5 hours including a BC Ferries crossing, either Horseshoe Bay to Nanaimo or Tsawwassen to Swartz Bay; Victoria is about 50 minutes south over the Malahat and Nanaimo about 45 minutes north, with the nearest airport at Nanaimo (YCD).

cells.v: Through a referral worker; office Mon to Fri 9am to 12pm, 1pm to 4pm

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's listing and its own website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: How much does Tsow-Tun Le Lum cost?
faqs.a: There is no per diem charge for First Nations people with Status and for recognized Inuit and Métis people who live in Canada, because the programs are funded by the First Nations Health Authority. Self-pay participants must pay in advance; call 250-390-3123 for the current daily rate. Travel to and from the centre is your own responsibility, though your Nation or FNHA may cover medical transportation.

faqs.q: Who can attend the Thuy Na Mut program?
faqs.a: Thuy Na Mut is for Indigenous people aged 19 and over who are struggling with the effects of substance use. Programs are co-ed and for individuals, so couples and families do not attend together. Applicants need a valid medical care card, stable health and no outstanding court matters.

Thuy Na Mut is a 6-week live-in program that starts on the Tuesday of the first week and ends on the Friday of the sixth. Our older listing described it as 40 days. The second stage Kwunatsustul trauma program runs 5 weeks and Honouring Grief runs 3 weeks.

faqs.q: Does Tsow-Tun Le Lum offer detox?
faqs.a: No. The centre has no medical staff and cannot support anyone going through withdrawal. You need at least two weeks free of alcohol and drugs before your intake date, and that includes methadone, suboxone and all cannabis products with THC or CBD.

faqs.q: How do I apply, and is there a wait list?
faqs.a: You apply through a referral worker such as a drug and alcohol counsellor, band social worker, therapist or doctor; the centre does not accept self-referrals. Your worker emails the intake package to info@ttlls.org. Once an application is approved the wait is usually three to six months, and incomplete packages take longer.

faqs.q: Where is Tsow-Tun Le Lum and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The centre is at 2850 Miller Road, just south of Duncan on Vancouver Island. Coming south from Nanaimo on Highway 1, turn right onto Miller Road across from The Old Farm Market; from Victoria, turn left. The building with the green roof is on the left after about 0.75 km. Nanaimo Airport (YCD) is the closest, and the centre does not pick people up there, so bring cash or a taxi voucher.

faqs.q: Is the centre still in Lantzville?
faqs.a: No. Tsow-Tun Le Lum operated in Snaw-Naw-As territory near Lantzville from 1988 until 2023. Since January 2024 its live-in programs have run from the new healing house on Cowichan lands in Duncan. The phone number, (250) 390-3123, is the same.

faqs.q: What will I do in treatment?
faqs.a: You take part in group and individual therapy led by the centre's professional team, along with cultural and spiritual healing led by Elders. That includes healing circles, sweat lodge, pipe ceremony, brushings, journal work, art and physical activity. Participation in ceremony is encouraged.

You leave with an aftercare plan you build during the program, and you keep seeing a counsellor at home who agreed to provide aftercare. Graduates of Thuy Na Mut can also join Nakalkala, an 8-week virtual group that meets up to three times a week.

Bring enough personal supplies for your whole stay, plus ID, bank cards and spending money. The centre keeps ID, cards and cash in a locked safe. You will also need your completed pre-admission medical, including a TB screening result from the last year.

faqs.q: Is there support if I need to talk to someone now?
faqs.a: Yes. The society runs a toll-free support line at 1-888-403-3123, open Monday to Friday 8am to 8pm and 10am to 2pm on weekends and holidays. Its Resolution Health Support Workers offer counselling and cultural support by phone, Zoom, FaceTime or Facebook to residential school survivors and their families.
